To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the wind climate of the north-west Atlantic is characterized by a high wind potential, especially in the winter months.

the wind climate in North Atlantic waters is suitable to support wind energy development and that the wind climate can be used as a criterion to assess the distance at which future offshore wind parks should be located.

1) The wind database can be used to assess the potential power output of wind parks and to derive the distance at which future parks should be placed in order to exhibit different wind climate characteristics; 2) Seasonal workability of offshore wind parks can be assessed by using wave data; and 3) The auxiliary data can aid the planning of offshore wind parks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
creating a WebGIS tool that provides a comprehensive environmental assessment for offshore wind parks.
the development of an integrated environmental database to support the planning of offshore wind parks.
the creation and use of environmental data in support of wind energy planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EnerGeo platform provides a valuable tool for the assessment of the environmental effects of wind energy and that it can serve as an example for the development of future platforms for the assessment of other sources of renewable energy.
the EnerGeo platform provides a valuable source of environmental data for the planning and assessment of offshore wind parks.
the environmental data created for the EnerGIO project are of high quality and provide a solid basis for further research on offshore wind energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EnerGIO client tool provides an integrated platform of environmental information for the planning of future offshore wind parks.

a 27 km resolution, 11 year wind database can be created using the WAM model and the WRF model can be used to assess the distance at which future offshore wind parks should be located to exhibit different wind regimes.
the EnerGeo PIA client tool provides an integrated platform for assessing the environmental impacts of offshore wind energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wind farms can be placed up to 100 km from the shore without a significant impact on the local climate.
wind parks in the North-West Atlantic should be placed 50–100 km offshore to achieve a stable wind regime and that the seasonal variability in wind speed is not as high as previously assumed.
the EnerGEROFF-Wind client tool is a powerful tool that can be used for the planning of future wind parks.
